solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Young lover’s house leased by top university (7)

indicators.note: 'by' means beside: LET sits next to CAP and U, here after them

blocks.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
U = university
let = leased, as a flat is let

annotation.surface: A property listing: a fashionable family home rented out to a leading university.
annotation.walkthrough: The young lover is Juliet, and her house in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet is the Capulets. 'House' means a family line, not a building.
annotation.definitionFit: The Capulets are Juliet's family, her 'house' in the dynastic sense.

clue.text: Dreary company? Don’t scowl so much! (10)

blocks.note: Co. = company
to lour is to scowl; not doing it so much is to lour less

annotation.surface: Someone stuck with gloomy companions begs them to stop frowning.
annotation.walkthrough: The instruction 'Don't scowl so much' is read as the phrase LOUR LESS. LOUR is an old word for scowl that crosswords love.
annotation.definitionFit: Colourless means dull and lacking interest, which is dreary.

clue.text: Heavy tools misspelt in a crumpled list (9,6)

indicators.note: a misspelt word has its letters wrong, so the letters that follow are to be rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: A workman's inventory of heavy equipment, badly spelt on a crumpled sheet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crumpled' looks like the anagram indicator, but it is part of the fodder; the instruction is 'misspelt', and all fifteen letters of 'in a crumpled list' are used.
annotation.definitionFit: Pneumatic drills are the heavy compressed-air tools that break up roads.

clue.text: Like a full ship that’s left port (5)

blocks.note: L = left
Aden is a port in Yemen

annotation.surface: A cargo ship, fully loaded, sailing out of harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left port' reads as a ship departing; it is L followed by a port, and ADEN is the crossword's favourite one.
annotation.definitionFit: A ship that is laden carries a full load of cargo.

clue.text: Most palatable wine is covered by tax (8)

indicators.note: the wine goes inside, with TEST covering it on both sides

blocks.note: to tax is to test, as a puzzle taxes the mind
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

annotation.surface: A complaint that the nicest wine carries the heaviest duty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks like duty on alcohol, but it means strain or test. ASTI is the usual crossword wine.
annotation.definitionFit: Tastiest means most pleasant to eat or drink, most palatable.

clue.text: Joints provided in some prosthetic limbs feel stiff at first (7)

indicators.note: IF goes inside the string of first letters
take the first letter of each word it governs

blocks.clueFragment: some prosthetic limbs feel stiff at first
blocks.note: S, P, L, F, S: the first letters of the five words
if = provided (that)

annotation.surface: An amputee's complaint that artificial limbs start out stiff at the joints.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joints' seems to be about knees and elbows in this surface; it is slang for cannabis cigarettes. IF slips in after the third initial.
annotation.definitionFit: Spliffs are cannabis cigarettes, commonly called joints.

clue.text: Spies turning up in old clubs (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to snoop is to spy

annotation.surface: Secret agents surfacing in old gentlemen's clubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests the London gentlemen's club, a favourite haunt of fictional spies; here they are golf clubs. A spoon was an old wooden club, roughly a modern three-wood.
annotation.definitionFit: The spoon was a lofted wooden golf club of the 19th century.

clue.text: Large copper in uniform heading for bogus judge’s study at night (9)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another, as a person is in a room, so CU sits inside U…B
the head, or first letter, of the next word

blocks.note: L = large
U = uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the first letter of Bogus
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate is to judge or assess

annotation.surface: A big policeman in uniform heads off to investigate a fake judge's study.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'uniform' paint a police officer; they are the element and the phonetic alphabet. 'Judge's study' reads as a room, but the 's is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: To lucubrate is to study or write laboriously, originally by lamplight at night.

clue.text: Tone of Tory supporting one’s plea to be recalled (6-2-3,4)

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporter sits underneath, so BLUE comes last

blocks.note: 'forget me not' is a plea to be remembered
blue is the Conservative (Tory) party colour

annotation.surface: A Conservative backing someone's appeal against a recall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' suggests a product recall or an MP being recalled; here it means remembered. A Tory is a British Conservative, whose colour is blue.
annotation.definitionFit: Forget-me-not blue is a pale sky blue, a shade or tone named after the flower.

clue.text: Band’s big hit millions ignored (4)

indicators.note: the M is left out of SMASH

blocks.note: a smash is a big hit, a smash hit
M = millions, removed

annotation.surface: A pop group's chart-topper, and the millions it earned, left unmentioned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' and 'big hit' make a pop group with a number one record; the band is a strip of cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder.

clue.text: Song, mostly fiction (3)

indicators.note: most of the word: drop its last letter

blocks.note: a German art song, as by Schubert, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A remark that most of a song's story is made up.
annotation.walkthrough: The song is a LIED (plural lieder), the German art song; 'mostly' docks its D.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an untruth is a piece of fiction.

clue.text: Parties entertaining northern banker throws (11)

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so DISCOS holds the rest

blocks.note: discos are dance parties
N = northern
a banker is a sure thing, a cert(ainty)

annotation.surface: A party host laying on entertainment for a banker from the north.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banker' reads as someone in finance; in betting slang it is a certainty, a cert. 'Throws' is a verb: it unsettles.
annotation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to disconcert or confuse them.

clue.text: Men’s linen about to be arranged in drawers (14)

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Laundry instructions: the men's linen to be sorted into chests of drawers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawers' looks like furniture to put linen in; it is underwear, and UNMENTIONABLES is the coy name for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Unmentionables is a humorous euphemism for underwear, as are drawers.

clue.text: A jolly old fellow’s battle against evil (10)

blocks.note: as written
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
aged = old
a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college

annotation.surface: A cheerful old man gearing up for a fight with the forces of darkness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A jolly old fellow' sounds like Old King Cole or Santa; each word is a separate piece. Jolly for a Royal Marine is old naval slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the final battle between good and evil foretold in Revelation.

clue.text: Rent small room someone vacated for free (3,5)

indicators.note: empty the word of its middle, keeping only its outer letters

blocks.note: to let is to rent out
the smallest room: the loo, a British word for toilet
SomeonE with its inside emptied

annotation.surface: An advert: a small room, left empty by its last tenant, available to rent at no cost.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a lettings notice, and 'free' seems to mean no charge; it is the verb, to release.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with 'free' as a verb: animals let loose from a pen have been freed.

clue.text: Disposed to shove or go too far (9)

indicators.note: disposed can mean arranged, as troops are disposed in battle order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone inclined either to push or to overstep the mark.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disposed to' reads as 'inclined to'; 'disposed' alone is the instruction, meaning arranged, and 'to' belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from aiming and landing: a pilot who overshoots the runway has gone past the mark.

clue.text: Pound of meat, paltry end cut (6)

indicators.note: its last letter is cut off

blocks.note: ham is a meat
MERE (paltry, as in 'a mere pittance') without its last letter

annotation.surface: A butcher weighing out a pound of meat and trimming a measly bit off the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pound of meat' reads as a weight; 'Pound' is the verb, to strike repeatedly.
annotation.definitionFit: To hammer is to pound, strike hard and repeatedly.

clue.text: Possible order for trio to hold melody back (8)

definitions.text: Possible order for trio to hold melody back

indicators.note: one possible ordering of the letters: an anagram

blocks.note: anagram fodder
a tune is a melody; anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A conductor's instruction to a trio to slow the melody.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: ritenuto is an Italian musical direction, an order to hold back. The wordplay rearranges TRIO with TUNE.
annotation.definitionFit: Ritenuto, marked on a score, tells players to hold back the tempo at once.

clue.text: One may hold coffee and walk nonchalantly, on a mobile (6)

indicators.note: a phone carries only the sound, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: to sashay is to walk in a casual, showy way

annotation.surface: Someone strolling along with a coffee in hand, chatting on their phone.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a coffee-to-go and a phone call; the coffee is instant in a little packet, and its name is pronounced 'sa-SHAY'.
annotation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed packet, such as one holding a portion of instant coffee.

clue.text: Ireland’s rupture brought about in Belfast originally (8)

indicators.note: HERNIA is brought round the letters, enclosing them
the original, first letters of 'in Belfast'

blocks.note: a hernia is a rupture
the first letters of In and Belfast

annotation.surface: A news line about a political rift in Ireland that began in Belfast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rupture' suggests a political split; it is a medical one. 'In' is part of the letter selection, not a container word.
annotation.definitionFit: The Latin name the Romans used for Ireland, still seen in poetry and on old maps.

clue.text: Figure seen in posh country houses (6)

indicators.note: STATE houses, or holds inside it, the U

blocks.note: a state is a country
U = upper-class, posh

annotation.surface: A sculpture on display in grand country houses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country houses' is a single idea in the surface, stately homes; split them and 'houses' becomes the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Figure in its sculptural sense, a carved or cast likeness of a person, which is what stands in a stately home.

clue.text: Understanding 60 per cent of these irritate, act decisively (5,3,6)

indicators.note: three of the five letters of THESE, the first three

blocks.note: a grasp of something is an understanding of it
the first 3 of the 5 letters of THESE
to nettle is to irritate

annotation.surface: Someone who gets why most of these people are annoyed, and acts.
annotation.walkthrough: A percentage in a clue asks for that share of a word's letters. To grasp the nettle is a British idiom: a nettle stings less if seized firmly.
annotation.definitionFit: To grasp the nettle is to tackle a difficulty boldly, acting decisively.

clue.text: Set off with no rescue boat and sink (5)

indicators.note: 'with no' means lacking, so the word is written without the ARK

blocks.note: embarked = set off on a journey
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood; removed

annotation.surface: A ship setting sail without a lifeboat, and going down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rescue boat' suggests a lifeboat; the one crosswords mean is Noah's ark.
annotation.definitionFit: To embed is to sink something firmly into a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Spruce border, cut back (4)

blocks.note: spruce as an adjective: neat and smart
a decorative edging on clothes or furniture
to prune a little, as with a hedge or hair

annotation.surface: Gardening advice: tidy the hedge of spruce along the border.
annotation.walkthrough: Three definitions, not two: neat, an edging, and to prune. The gardening surface makes 'Spruce' a tree and 'border' a flowerbed.
annotation.definitionFit: Trim means neat (spruce), a decorative edging (border), and to cut back.

clue.text: Governance by one on hand to give guidance (4,2,5)

blocks.note: rule = governance
of = by, as in 'a play of Shakespeare'
the thumb is one digit on the hand

annotation.surface: An official on hand to advise on the rules.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On hand' reads as available; it is literal, a digit on the hand.
annotation.definitionFit: A rule of thumb is a rough practical guide, a piece of guidance.

clue.text: Top firm? Not really (3)

indicators.note: the SO is not there: remove it

blocks.note: solid = firm
so = really, as in 'so good'; removed

annotation.surface: Doubt whether a company is really a leading firm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top firm' reads as a leading company, and 'Not really' as a shrug; the question mark hints at the break between them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the cover of a jar or box is its top.

clue.text: Bagpipe songs to be played amid silence (7)

indicators.note: SET goes amid, in the middle of, MUTE

blocks.note: to silence is to mute
a band's set is the songs it plays in a performance

annotation.surface: A piper's playlist to be performed in a hushed hall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Silence' reads as a hushed audience, but it is the verb, to make quiet. A band's 'set' is the list of songs it plays in one performance.
annotation.definitionFit: A musette is a small French bagpipe popular in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Look around and be curious, dear fellow (3,4)

indicators.note: 'around' means turned round to face the other way, so the word reads backwards
curious can mean odd, so the letters of 'and be' come out strangely

blocks.note: lo = look, as in 'lo and behold', turned around
anagram of AND BE

annotation.surface: Someone nosy is told to have a look about, with a chummy 'my dear fellow'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link word; it is fodder. 'Old bean' is dated British upper-class slang for a friend.
annotation.definitionFit: Old bean is a jocular, old-fashioned British term of address, like 'dear fellow'.
